abstract_sentences.text: Transformer-based models have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of domains, yet our understanding of their training dynamics remains limited.
qualifiers: across a wide range of domains

evidence.anchor: our understanding of their training dynamics remains limited

abstract_sentences.text: In this work, we identify a recurrent focus–dilution cycle in attention learning and provide a rigorous explanation in a one-layer Transformer setting for Markovian data via gradient-flow analysis.
abstract_sentences.transition: answers the gap with the study setting

evidence.anchor: a recurrent focus–dilution cycle in attention learning

abstract_sentences.text: Using stage-wise linearization around critical points, we show that a single focus–dilution cycle can be decomposed into a sequence of distinct stages.
abstract_sentences.transition: turns the idea into an analyzable sequence

abstract_sentences.text: First, embedding and projection rapidly condense to a rank-one structure, while attention parameters remain effectively frozen.
Then, the attention parameters begin to increase, inducing a frequency-driven focus toward high-frequency tokens.
As attention continues to evolve, it generates next-order perturbations in embeddings, leading to a mass-redistribution mechanism that progressively dilutes this focus.
abstract_sentences.comparison: formed focus versus later diluted focus

abstract_sentences.text: Finally, small asymmetries among low-frequency tokens lift a degenerate critical point, opening new embedding directions and initiating the next cycle.
Experiments on synthetic Markovian data as well as WikiText and TinyStories corroborate the predicted stages and cyclical dynamics.
abstract_sentences.comparison: synthetic Markovian versus two real corpora

experimental_design.name: formal_research_questions
experimental_design.description: Section 4 has no enumerated research questions or predeclared hypotheses; it frames experiments as validation of the four theoretical stages.

experimental_design.name: population_theory_setting
experimental_design.description: Theory uses a one-layer Transformer, cross-entropy, population gradient flow, small initialization, and Markov data with one high-frequency token plus low-frequency tokens.

evidence.anchor: We therefore study a one-layer Transformer

experimental_design.name: synthetic_data
experimental_design.description: Main text describes four transition matrices sharing π=(0.75,0.19,0.05,0.01); Appendix E reports exponential π0, λ=0.8, length 20, and 100,000 sequences.

experimental_design.name: model_and_training
experimental_design.description: Appendix E specifies m=256, independent N(0,1/m²) initialization, Adam with 1.5×10⁻⁴ learning rate, and no learning-rate scheduler.

evidence.anchor: Adam optimizer with a fixed learning rate

experimental_design.name: mechanism_measurements
experimental_design.description: Measures include neuron input-weight cosine similarity, PCA over embedding snapshots, attention maps, attention entropy, embedding norm, and a perpendicular projection norm.

evidence.anchor: cosine similarity between neuronal input weights

experimental_design.name: real_world_data_and_selection
experimental_design.description: WikiText and TinyStories use the same simplified architecture and consistent hyperparameters; analysis tracks three most frequent tokens plus three randomly sampled medium-frequency tokens above 10% frequency.

experimental_design.name: controls_and_matching
experimental_design.description: Four synthetic transition matrices are said to share a stationary distribution; the real-data setting keeps architecture and hyperparameters consistent with synthetic experiments.

experimental_design.name: baselines
experimental_design.description: No competing model, alternate optimizer, ablated mechanism, or numerical baseline is reported in Section 4.

experimental_design.name: seeds_and_replicates
experimental_design.description: No random seed, independent-run count, or replicate aggregation is specified in the main experiments or Appendix E.

experimental_design.name: hardware_and_implementation_source

experimental_design.name: training_budget

claim_closure.claim: Attention learning contains a recurrent focus–dilution cycle in a minimal tractable setting.
claim_closure.method_response: Sections 2–3 define the Markov/one-layer gradient flow and derive four stages.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 2 shows the stages synthetically; Figure 3 shows analogous selected real-data signatures.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion restates the recurring cycle and limits formal scope.

claim_closure.claim: Stage-wise linearization around critical points explains initial condensation, focus, dilution, and the next direction.
claim_closure.method_response: Lemma 3.1 and Theorems 3.2, 3.5, 3.7, 3.9 provide the stage chain under stated assumptions.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 2 maps observable signatures to each stage.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion names rank-one condensation, saddle transitions, and symmetry breaking.

claim_closure.claim: The predicted cycle persists on synthetic Markov data and realistic data.
claim_closure.method_response: The theory predicts stage signatures but does not formally cover natural language corpora.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Synthetic and selected WikiText/TinyStories visualizations are provided without replicate statistics.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion calls real-corpus signatures qualitative and the framework a useful lens.

claim_closure.claim: Low-frequency asymmetry lifts degeneracy and starts a new embedding direction.
claim_closure.method_response: Theorem 3.9 proves an approximate critical point and a conditional Θ(δ) transverse instability for d=3.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 2 shows new directions but does not manipulate or sweep δ.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion recovers symmetry breaking as part of the framework.

claim_closure.claim: The Markov synthetic setting is a suitable proxy for early real-world attention dynamics.
claim_closure.method_response: The mechanism is derived only in the Markov/one-layer setting.
claim_closure.evidence_response: The evidence is token-level real-corpus visualization rather than a direct proxy comparison.

measurement_disagreements.name: automatic_numbered_equations
measurement_disagreements.description: The automatic draft counted 225 numbered equations. Manual physical-page census finds contiguous labels (1) through (230), including Eq. (1) on p.2 and Eq. (230) on p.54.

measurement_disagreements.name: synthetic_stationary_distribution
measurement_disagreements.description: Main §4.1 states π=(0.75,0.19,0.05,0.01), while Appendix E.1 specifies normalized exponential π0=(1/2,1/4,…,1/2^d). For d=4 these are not equal, and the PDF does not resolve which generated Figure 2.

measurement_disagreements.name: appendix_d_section_reference
measurement_disagreements.description: Appendix D is headed as details for Sec. 3.4, but its opening prose says it provides proofs for Section 4.4. The cited content is the asymmetry result of §3.4, so this is an internal section-number mismatch.

statistics.aggregation_unit: training-step trajectories for parameter/token observables; synthetic data has N=100,000 sequences, but per-curve run/seed denominator is not reported.
statistics.figure_caption_interpretability: Figures 2–3 explain their panels and stages, but do not report replication or uncertainty handling.

rhetoric.strength_balance: Strong verbs support conditional theory in §3; real-data claims use similar, preliminary, indirectly validate, and hypothesize.

final_judgment.single_storyline: π-driven rank-one condensation freezes attention; a saddle then creates high-frequency focus; embedding mass redistribution dilutes it; low-frequency asymmetry releases a transverse new direction and permits another cycle.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The one-layer Markov setup, Eqs. (1)–(24), the four-stage conceptual map, named theorems, three cross-column figures, real-data visual signatures, and a standalone Limitation section remain in the main body.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A holds related work; B–D hold nearly all proofs and Eqs. (25)–(230); E holds synthetic settings and analysis-tool definitions. This preserves conceptual self-sufficiency but does not fully close experimental reproducibility.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 precommits to a four-stage causal map, then §3 results and Figure 2 panels recover each stage in order.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The empirical mechanism claims have no replicate-level uncertainty, baseline/alternative-mechanism tests, or δ sweep; the main-text and Appendix-E stationary distributions also conflict without resolution.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a dynamics paper, align each theoretical transition with a named observable signature and a dedicated graphic readout before moving long proofs to the appendix.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This organization is most useful when a mechanism predicts an ordered trajectory. It does not replace fair baselines, uncertainty reporting, or broad external validation for performance- or deployment-centered claims.
